rulers.title: Dictators of the Roman Republic
rulers.note: From Broughton, MRR, with the causa as reported in the sources; where none is recorded rei gerundae is usually inferred. Years are Varronian; before c. 300 BC they run some years ahead of true dates and the earliest names are traditional. The 'dictator years' 333, 324, 309, 301 of the Fasti Capitolini are not real years. 'id' links known people.

list.name: Titus Larcius Flavus
list.note: First dictator by Livy's preferred tradition (2.18); others named Manius Valerius. Threat from the Latins and Sabines. Dates of the earliest dictatorships are traditional.

list.name: Aulus Postumius Albus Regillensis
list.note: Victory over the Latins at Lake Regillus, where the Dioscuri reportedly fought for Rome (Livy dates it 499 or 496); vowed the temple of Castor.

list.name: Manius Valerius Volusus Maximus
list.note: Appointed during the debt crisis of the First Secession of the plebs; campaigned against the Sabines and resigned when the Senate rejected debt relief.

list.name: Gaius Aemilius Mamercus
list.note: Doubtful: inferred by Bendel from Lydus' 'dictator in the 48th year of the Republic' and the plague precedent invoked in 363; Broughton thinks Lydus confused an interrex.

list.name: Lucius Quinctius Cincinnatus
list.note: Called from his four-iugera farm across the Tiber to rescue the consul Minucius trapped by the Aequi on Mount Algidus; triumphed and resigned after 16 days (Livy 3.26-29).

list.name: Lucius Quinctius Cincinnatus
list.note: Second dictatorship, against the alleged regal ambitions of the grain-dealer Spurius Maelius, whom Ahala killed in the Forum. The story is probably an aetiology of the Aequimaelium.

list.name: Mamercus Aemilius Mamercinus
list.note: War with Fidenae and Veii after the murder of Roman envoys by Lars Tolumnius; Aulus Cornelius Cossus won the spolia opima.

list.name: Quintus Servilius Priscus Fidenas
list.note: Capture of Fidenae.

list.name: Mamercus Aemilius Mamercinus
list.note: Second dictatorship; reportedly carried a law limiting the censorship to 18 months.

list.name: Aulus Postumius Tubertus
list.note: Victory over Aequi and Volsci at Mount Algidus; said to have executed his son for leaving his post.

list.name: Mamercus Aemilius Mamercinus
list.note: Third dictatorship; final war with Fidenae, which was destroyed.

list.name: Quintus Servilius Priscus Fidenas
list.note: Second dictatorship; war with the Aequi; capture of Labici.

list.name: Publius Cornelius Rutilus Cossus
list.note: War with the Volsci and Aequi at Antium.

list.name: Marcus Furius Camillus
list.note: Captured Veii after the ten-year siege, reportedly by a tunnel under the temple of Juno; evocatio of Juno Regina to the Aventine.

list.name: Marcus Furius Camillus
list.note: Second dictatorship (Varronian 390 = c. 387/386): named in exile at Ardea after the Gallic sack; the tale of his rescuing the ransom gold ('non auro sed ferro') is later embroidery (Polybius knows the Gauls left with the gold).

list.name: Marcus Furius Camillus
list.note: Third dictatorship; victories over Volsci, Aequi and Etruscans.

list.name: Aulus Cornelius Cossus
list.note: War with the Volsci; imprisonment of Marcus Manlius Capitolinus for agitation over debt.

list.name: Titus Quinctius Cincinnatus Capitolinus
list.note: Victory over the Praenestines at the Allia; captured nine towns.

list.name: Marcus Furius Camillus
list.note: Fourth dictatorship; used against the Licinio-Sextian agitation; abdicated.

list.name: Publius Manlius Capitolinus
list.causa: seditionis sedandae et rei gerundae causa
list.note: Named a plebeian as magister equitum, a concession to the Licinio-Sextian movement.

list.name: Marcus Furius Camillus
list.note: Fifth dictatorship; defeated the Gauls near Alba; reconciled the orders and vowed the temple of Concord as the Licinio-Sextian laws opened the consulship to plebeians.

list.name: Lucius Manlius Capitolinus Imperiosus
list.note: Appointed to drive the nail in the Capitoline temple to end a plague; tried to wage war instead and was forced to resign.

list.name: Appius Claudius Crassus Regillensis
list.note: Victory over the Hernici. The magister's name is preserved in the Fasti only as SCA[.]VLA.

list.name: Titus Quinctius Pennus Capitolinus Crispinus
list.note: Gallic war: the single combat of Titus Manlius, who took the torque of a giant Gaul and the cognomen Torquatus.

list.name: Quintus Servilius Ahala
list.note: Defeated the Gauls at the Colline Gate.

list.name: Gaius Sulpicius Peticus
list.note: Victory over the Gauls.

list.name: Gaius Marcius Rutilus
list.note: First plebeian dictator; defeated the Etruscans and triumphed by vote of the people over the Senate's objection.

list.name: Titus Manlius Imperiosus Torquatus
list.note: War against Caere, which was granted a 100-year truce.

list.name: Gaius Julius Iulus
list.note: Rumoured Etruscan war; tried to secure two patrician consuls.

list.name: Marcus Fabius Ambustus
list.note: Held elections amid the patrician-plebeian struggle over the consulship.

list.name: Titus Manlius Imperiosus Torquatus
list.note: Second dictatorship.

list.name: Gaius Claudius Crassinus Regillensis (?)
list.note: Names missing from the Fasti and not stated by any ancient author.

list.name: Lucius Furius Camillus
list.note: Second dictatorship; war against the Aurunci; vowed the temple of Juno Moneta on the Arx.

list.name: Publius Valerius Poplicola
list.note: Appointed to institute a festival after prodigies (a rain of stones, darkness by day).

list.name: Marcus Valerius Corvus
list.note: Mutiny of the garrison of Campania; Corvus negotiated, and the leges Genuciae followed.

list.name: Lucius Papirius Crassus
list.note: Latin War; operations against Antium.

list.name: Quintus Publilius Philo
list.note: Carried the leges Publiliae: plebiscites binding on all, patrum auctoritas given in advance for centuriate laws, one censor to be plebeian.

list.name: Gaius Claudius Inregillensis
list.note: Abdicated, appointment found vitiated.

list.name: Publius Cornelius Rufinus
list.note: Abdicated on a religious flaw. The Fasti list 333 as the first of four 'dictator years' (333, 324, 309, 301) with a dictator and no consuls; Livy places these dictators under the preceding consuls. The dictator years are a later chronographic insertion.

list.name: Marcus Papirius Crassus
list.note: Gallic scare.

list.name: Gnaeus Quinctilius Varus
list.note: Nail-driving after the 'poisoning' scandal in which 170 matrons were condemned (Livy 8.18). Name possibly Gnaeus Quinctius Capitolinus.

list.name: Marcus Claudius Marcellus
list.note: Abdicated, appointment declared vitiated by the augurs.

list.name: Lucius Papirius Cursor
list.note: Second Samnite War. Papirius tried to execute his magister equitum Fabius for fighting (and winning) against orders; the people and Senate interceded (Livy 8.30-35). 324 is the second dictator year.

list.name: Aulus Cornelius Cossus Arvina
list.causa: rei gerundae or ludorum faciendorum causa
list.note: Sources conflict; most historians think he presided at the Ludi Romani when the praetor fell ill.

list.name: Quintus Fabius Ambustus
list.note: Abdicated on a flaw, in the year of the Caudine Forks.

list.name: Gaius Maenius
list.note: Livy describes an inquiry into conspiracies; causa disputed.

list.name: Titus Manlius Imperiosus Torquatus
list.note: Third dictatorship.

list.name: Lucius Aemilius Mamercinus Privernas
list.note: Second dictatorship; siege of Saticula.

list.name: Quintus Fabius Maximus Rullianus
list.magisterEquitum: Quintus Aulius Cerretanus; Gaius Fabius Ambustus
list.note: Defeat at Lautulae, where the magister equitum Aulius fell; replaced by Gaius Fabius.

list.name: Gaius Maenius
list.note: Second dictatorship; inquiry into Capuan conspiracy.

list.name: Gaius Poetelius Libo Visolus
list.note: Capture of Nola per Livy and the Fasti; an alternative tradition makes him dictator clavi figendi causa, and Diodorus credits the victories to Quintus Fabius.

list.name: Gaius Sulpicius Longus
list.note: Livy instead names Junius Bubulcus dictator.

list.name: Lucius Papirius Cursor
list.note: Second dictatorship; great victory over the Samnites, whose gilded shields were displayed in the Forum (Livy 9.40). 309 is the third dictator year.

list.name: Gaius Junius Bubulcus Brutus
list.note: War with the Aequi, subdued in eight days (Livy 10.1).

list.name: Marcus Valerius Corvus
list.magisterEquitum: Quintus Fabius Maximus Rullianus (?) or Marcus Aemilius Paullus (?)
list.note: Second dictatorship; Etruscans and Marsi. 301 is the fourth and last dictator year.

list.name: Quintus Hortensius
list.note: Appointed during the last secession of the plebs (to the Janiculum); carried the lex Hortensia making plebiscites binding on the whole people. Died in office.

list.name: Appius Claudius Caecus (?)
list.note: Possibly dictator suffectus after Hortensius' death (Mommsen); known only from the elogium of Appius, which credits him with a dictatorship.

list.name: Marcus Aemilius Barbula (?)
list.note: Known only from literary sources; Broughton dates him 292-285.

list.name: Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus Maximus
list.note: Also the first plebeian censor to close a lustrum (280).

list.name: Publius Cornelius Rufinus (?)
list.note: Date uncertain (Broughton 292-285; Niebuhr 280, after Heraclea).

list.name: Gnaeus Fulvius Maximus Centumalus
list.note: Nail-driving during the First Punic War.

list.name: Quintus Ogulnius Gallus
list.note: To celebrate the Latin Festival on the Alban Mount in the consuls' absence.

list.name: Marcus Claudius Glicia
list.note: Named in contempt by the consul Publius Claudius Pulcher after his defeat at Drepana; a freedman's son and scribe, he was forced to resign but kept the right to the toga praetexta.

list.name: Aulus Atilius Calatinus
list.note: First dictator to command an army outside Italy (Sicily).

list.name: Tiberius Coruncanius
list.note: First plebeian pontifex maximus.

list.name: Gaius Duilius
list.note: Victor of Mylae (260), the first Roman naval triumph.

list.name: Quintus Fabius Maximus Verrucosus
list.note: Date inferred (Broughton): Livy calls 217 Fabius' second dictatorship, so a first must fall in the gap of 221-219. Plutarch (Marc. 5) tells of a dictator Minucius with Flaminius as magister who abdicated because a shrew squeaked, which may be the same episode.

list.name: Quintus Fabius Maximus Verrucosus
list.note: Elected by the people after Trasimene (Livy calls him prodictator). His delaying strategy earned him the name Cunctator; a plebiscite of the tribune Metilius gave Minucius equal imperium, the only time two dictators served together.

list.name: Lucius Veturius Philo
list.note: Abdicated after 14 days on a flaw.

list.name: Marcus Junius Pera
list.note: After Cannae; enrolled 8,000 slaves (volones), debtors and convicts, and took arms from the temples.

list.name: Marcus Fabius Buteo
list.note: Unique causa: named, without a magister equitum, to fill the Senate's 177 vacancies after Cannae; resigned the same day (Livy 23.22-23). Two dictators held office simultaneously.

list.name: Quintus Fulvius Flaccus
list.note: Nominated by the consul Laevinus amid a quarrel over the right of nomination.

list.name: Titus Manlius Torquatus
list.causa: comitiorum habendorum et ludorum faciendorum causa
list.note: After the death of the consul Marcellus in an ambush near Venusia.

list.name: Marcus Livius Salinator
list.note: Victor of the Metaurus that year.

list.name: Gaius Servilius Geminus
list.note: Last traditional dictatorship; the office then lapsed for 120 years, replaced in emergencies by the senatus consultum ultimum.

list.name: Lucius Cornelius Sulla Felix
list.causa: legibus scribundis et rei publicae constituendae causa
list.note: Appointed under the lex Valeria proposed by the interrex Flaccus, without time limit. Used it for proscriptions and a constitutional overhaul (courts to senators, tribunate gutted, Senate doubled to c. 600, 20 quaestors). Resigned probably early 79 (or 81).

list.name: Gaius Julius Caesar
list.note: First dictatorship, 11 days, named by the praetor Lepidus under a special law to hold the consular elections; also passed debt and amnesty measures.

list.name: Gaius Julius Caesar
list.note: Second dictatorship (Oct 48 to late 47), voted after Pharsalus.

list.name: Gaius Julius Caesar
list.note: Third dictatorship, voted after Thapsus in April 46 for ten years, renewed annually.

list.name: Gaius Julius Caesar
list.magisterEquitum: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus (designated: Gaius Octavius; Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus, non iniit)
list.note: Perpetual dictator from c. Feb 44 (DICT PERPETVO on coins); assassinated 15 Mar 44. The lex Antonia then abolished the dictatorship for ever; Augustus refused it in 22 BC.

rulers.title: Censors (pairs per censorship)
rulers.note: Year of election (lustrum normally closed within 18 months). From Broughton, MRR. Several censorships ended without a lustrum (marked in notes). Imperial entries show the absorption of the office.

list.name: Lucius Papirius Mugillanus and Lucius Sempronius Atratinus
list.note: First censors, created to relieve the consuls (or consular tribunes) of the census (Livy 4.8). Both patrician.

list.name: Gaius Furius Paculus Fusus and Marcus Geganius Macerinus
list.note: Built the Villa Publica on the Campus Martius, where the census was taken.

list.name: Lucius Papirius Crassus (?) and Publius Pinarius Mamercinus (?)
list.note: Uncertain pair.

list.name: Lucius Papirius Mugillanus and unknown
list.note: Mugillanus' second censorship.

list.name: Marcus Furius Camillus and Marcus Postumius Albinus Regillensis
list.note: Imposed a tax on bachelors (aes uxorium) per Valerius Maximus and Plutarch.

list.name: Lucius Papirius Cursor and Gaius Julius Iullus
list.note: Julius died in office and Marcus Cornelius Maluginensis was elected suffect; Rome was taken by the Gauls during that lustrum, after which a censor's death in office required both to resign.

list.name: Marcus Furius Fusus (?) and Lucius Papirius Mugillanus (?)
list.note: Uncertain.

list.name: Spurius Postumius Albinus Regillensis and Gaius Sulpicius Camerinus
list.note: Postumius died; no suffect appointed, the censors resigned and the census lapsed.

list.name: Spurius Servilius Priscus and Quintus Cloelius Siculus
list.note: Census impeded by war and debt agitation.

list.name: Gaius Sulpicius Peticus and Postumius Regillensis Albinus (?)
Marcus Fabius Ambustus and Lucius Furius Medullinus
Gnaeus Manlius Capitolinus Imperiosus and Gaius Marcius Rutilus
list.note: Marcius was the first plebeian censor.

list.name: Lucius Cornelius Scipio and Publius Cornelius Scipio (?)
Spurius Postumius Albinus Caudinus and Quintus Publilius Philo
list.note: Enrolled new citizens in two new tribes (Maecia and Scaptia).

list.name: Lucius Papirius Crassus and Gaius Maenius
list.note: Two new tribes (Oufentina and Falerna).

list.name: Appius Claudius Caecus and Gaius Plautius Venox
list.note: Built the Via Appia and the Aqua Appia; distributed the humiles across all tribes and enrolled freedmen's sons in the Senate; Appius held on beyond 18 months, allegedly for five years.

list.name: Marcus Valerius Maximus Corvinus and Gaius Junius Bubulcus Brutus
list.note: Built roads across the ager Romanus at public expense.

list.name: Quintus Fabius Maximus Rullianus and Publius Decius Mus
list.note: Confined freedmen and the urban poor to the four urban tribes; instituted the transvectio equitum (15 July parade of the equites).

list.name: Publius Sulpicius Saverrio and Publius Sempronius Sophus
list.note: Two new tribes (Aniensis and Terentina, 299).

list.name: Publius Cornelius Arvina and Gaius Marcius Rutilus Censorinus
list.note: Census of 262,321 citizens (Livy 10.47).

list.name: Quintus Fabius Maximus Gurges (?) and Spurius Carvilius Maximus (?)
list.note: Uncertain.

list.name: Lucius Cornelius Scipio Barbatus and Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus Maximus
list.note: Domitius was the first plebeian censor to perform the lustrum.

list.name: Quintus Aemilius Papus and Gaius Fabricius Luscinus
list.note: Fabricius expelled the ex-consul and ex-dictator Publius Cornelius Rufinus from the Senate for owning ten pounds of silver plate.

list.name: Lucius Papirius Praetextatus and Manius Curius Dentatus
list.note: Curius began the Anio Vetus aqueduct from the spoils of Pyrrhus.

list.name: Lucius Aemilius Barbula and Quintus Marcius Philippus
Gnaeus Cornelius Blasio and Gaius Marcius Rutilus Censorinus
list.note: The only man censor twice; he then carried a law forbidding iteration, earning the cognomen Censorinus. Census 292,234.

list.name: Lucius Cornelius Scipio and Gaius Duilius
Lucius Postumius Megellus and Decimus Junius Pera
list.note: Postumius died in office; the censors resigned.

list.name: Manius Valerius Maximus Corvinus Messalla and Publius Sempronius Sophus
list.note: Demoted 400 equites who had disobeyed orders in Sicily to aerarii.

list.name: Aulus Manlius Torquatus Atticus and Aulus Atilius Calatinus
list.note: Census 241,712, showing First Punic War losses.

list.name: Marcus Fabius Buteo and Gaius Aurelius Cotta
list.note: Two last tribes (Velina and Quirina), bringing the total to 35.

list.name: Lucius Cornelius Lentulus Caudinus and Quintus Lutatius Cerco
list.note: Lutatius died in office.

list.name: Aulus Postumius Albinus and Gaius Atilius Bulbus
list.note: Census 270,713.

list.name: Titus Manlius Torquatus and Quintus Fulvius Flaccus
list.note: Resigned on a flaw in their election.

list.name: Quintus Fabius Maximus Verrucosus and Marcus Sempronius Tuditanus
Gaius Claudius Centho and Marcus Junius Pera
list.note: Did not complete the lustrum.

list.name: Lucius Aemilius Papus and Gaius Flaminius
list.note: Flaminius built the Via Flaminia and the Circus Flaminius; freedmen restricted to four urban tribes.

list.name: Publius Furius Philus and Marcus Atilius Regulus
list.note: Punished Cannae survivors who planned to leave Italy and men who broke their oath to Hannibal; Furius died before the lustrum.

list.name: Lucius Veturius Philo and Publius Licinius Crassus Dives
list.note: Veturius died; Licinius resigned.

list.name: Marcus Cornelius Cethegus and Publius Sempronius Tuditanus
list.note: Census 137,108, the low point after Cannae (Livy 27.36).

list.name: Gaius Claudius Nero and Marcus Livius Salinator
list.note: The victors of the Metaurus degraded each other (each deprived the other of his public horse); introduced the salt tax.

list.name: Publius Cornelius Scipio Africanus and Publius Aelius Paetus
list.note: Scipio named princeps senatus.

list.name: Gaius Cornelius Cethegus and Sextus Aelius Paetus Catus
list.note: Separate seats for senators at the Ludi Romani.

list.name: Titus Quinctius Flamininus and Marcus Claudius Marcellus
list.note: Census 258,318 after the enfranchisement of the Campanians as census-registered.

list.name: Lucius Valerius Flaccus and Marcus Porcius Cato
list.note: Cato's famously severe censorship: expelled Lucius Flamininus from the Senate, taxed luxury at ten times assessed value, built the Basilica Porcia, cut off private diversions of public water.

list.name: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus and Marcus Fulvius Nobilior
list.note: Reconciled at the Senate's urging; Basilica Aemilia (Fulvia) and the first stone piers of the Pons Aemilius; changed voting in the tribes by property and occupation.

list.name: Aulus Postumius Albinus Luscus and Quintus Fulvius Flaccus
list.note: Fulvius stripped the marble roof tiles of the temple of Juno Lacinia at Croton for his temple of Fortuna Equestris and was forced to return them; paved streets in Rome.

list.name: Gaius Claudius Pulcher and Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus
list.note: Clashed with the publicani and survived prosecution by a tribune; freedmen confined to one urban tribe (Esquilina); Basilica Sempronia.

list.name: Lucius Aemilius Paullus Macedonicus and Quintus Marcius Philippus
list.note: Philippus set up a sundial; census 337,022 (Per. 46).

list.name: Publius Cornelius Scipio Nasica Corculum and Marcus Popillius Laenas
list.note: Removed unauthorised statues from the Forum; Nasica set up the first water-clock in Rome.

list.name: Marcus Valerius Messalla and Gaius Cassius Longinus
list.note: Their stone theatre was demolished on Nasica's motion (151) as harmful to morals.

list.name: Lucius Cornelius Lentulus Lupus and Lucius Marcius Censorinus
Publius Cornelius Scipio Aemilianus and Lucius Mummius Achaicus
list.note: Aemilianus reportedly changed the lustral prayer from asking the gods to increase Rome's possessions to preserving them (Val. Max. 4.1.10); Mummius was the lenient colleague.

list.name: Appius Claudius Pulcher and Quintus Fulvius Nobilior
list.note: Claudius, father-in-law of Tiberius Gracchus, was princeps senatus.

list.name: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Macedonicus and Quintus Pompeius
list.note: First pair both plebeian. Metellus' speech urging marriage (de prole augenda) was later read out by Augustus.

list.name: Gnaeus Servilius Caepio and Lucius Cassius Longinus Ravilla
list.note: Censured Marcus Aemilius Lepidus Porcina for renting a house at 6,000 sesterces; census 394,736.

list.name: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Balearicus and Lucius Calpurnius Piso Frugi
Lucius Caecilius Metellus Diadematus and Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus
list.note: Expelled 32 senators.

list.name: Marcus Aemilius Scaurus and Marcus Livius Drusus
list.note: Drusus died in office; Scaurus refused to resign until forced; built the Via Aemilia Scauri and the Pons Mulvius in stone.

list.name: Quintus Fabius Maximus Eburnus and Gaius Licinius Geta
Quintus Caecilius Metellus Numidicus and Gaius Caecilius Metellus Caprarius
list.note: Metellus Numidicus tried to expel Saturninus and Glaucia from the Senate and refused to enrol the pretended son of Tiberius Gracchus.

list.name: Lucius Valerius Flaccus and Marcus Antonius
list.note: Antonius the orator; expelled the tribune Duronius from the Senate.

list.name: Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus and Lucius Licinius Crassus
list.note: Edict against the Latin rhetoricians (Gellius 15.11); quarrelled bitterly (Crassus' lampreys); no lustrum.

list.name: Lucius Julius Caesar and Publius Licinius Crassus
list.note: Charged with enrolling the new citizens of the Social War in a limited number of tribes; no lustrum.

list.name: Lucius Marcius Philippus and Marcus Perperna
list.note: Under the Cinnan regime; census 463,000. No further censors until 70.

list.name: Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus Clodianus and Lucius Gellius Publicola
list.note: Restored the censorship after Sulla; expelled 64 senators; census 910,000 reflecting the post-Social War enfranchisement of Italy.

list.name: Marcus Licinius Crassus and Quintus Lutatius Catulus
list.note: Deadlocked over Crassus' plan to enrol the Transpadani and annex Egypt; both resigned.

list.name: unknown and Lucius Aurelius Cotta
list.note: Obstructed by tribunes; resigned.

list.name: Lucius Julius Caesar (?) and Gaius Scribonius Curio (?)
list.note: Names uncertain.

list.name: Marcus Valerius Messalla Niger and Publius Servilius Vatia Isauricus
list.note: No lustrum.

list.name: Appius Claudius Pulcher and Lucius Calpurnius Piso Caesoninus
list.note: Appius purged the Senate (expelling Sallust); the last Republican censorship before the civil war.

list.name: Publius Sulpicius Rufus and Gaius Antonius Hybrida
list.note: Appointed under the triumvirs; no lustrum.

list.name: Imperator Caesar (Octavian) and Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa
list.note: Not censors but consuls with censoria potestas; first lustrum in 41 years; revised the Senate from c. 1,000 to 800; census 4,063,000 (RG 8).

list.name: Paullus Aemilius Lepidus and Lucius Munatius Plancus
list.note: The last private pair of censors; quarrelled, achieved nothing (Velleius 2.95).

list.name: Augustus (consulari imperio, alone)
list.note: Second census of Augustus; 4,233,000 citizens.

list.name: Augustus and Tiberius
list.note: Census completed by consular imperium shortly before Augustus' death; 4,937,000 citizens.

list.name: Claudius and Lucius Vitellius
list.note: Emperor took the title censor; census of 5,984,072 citizens (Tac. Ann. 11.25); admitted Gallic notables (Aedui) to the Senate (Lyon tablet).

list.name: Vespasian and Titus
list.note: Last formal census of Roman citizens; adlected new senatorial and patrician families.

list.name: Domitian
list.note: Took the title censor perpetuus, which no later emperor used; censorial functions absorbed into imperial power.
